candidate.blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance → Health Promotion/Disease Prevention: promote appropriate physical activity, rehabilitation participation, risk-factor reduction, and long-term health-maintenance behaviors for clients with chronic disease.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — cardiac rehabilitation and secondary prevention in stable heart failure
candidate.educational_objective: Explain that cardiac rehabilitation is an evidence-based secondary-prevention strategy for appropriate stable heart-failure clients that improves functional capacity and quality of life and can reduce heart-failure hospitalization without replacing medical therapy.

options.A: Cardiac rehabilitation can improve functional capacity, exercise tolerance, and health-related quality of life and may reduce heart-failure hospitalization in appropriate clients.
options.B: Cardiac rehabilitation is intended mainly for clients recovering from myocardial infarction and has little role in stable heart failure.
options.C: The main effect of cardiac rehabilitation in heart failure is to increase symptoms temporarily without meaningful functional benefit.
options.D: Cardiac rehabilitation replaces guideline-directed heart-failure medications once exercise training begins.

candidate.rationale: The AHA/ACC/HFSA heart-failure guideline reports that exercise training and exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation in medically stable heart-failure populations improve functional capacity, exercise tolerance, and health-related quality of life, and meta-analyses suggest reduced heart-failure hospitalization. The 2024 AHA/AACVPR cardiac-rehabilitation scientific statement explicitly includes stable heart failure among indications for cardiac rehabilitation. Therefore, A is correct. B incorrectly excludes heart failure, C contradicts documented functional and quality-of-life benefits, and D misrepresents cardiac rehabilitation as a replacement for guideline-directed medical therapy.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Directly supports cardiac rehabilitation for stable heart failure and its benefits for functional capacity, exercise tolerance, quality of life, and heart-failure hospitalization while not requiring a heart-failure-specific mortality claim.
candidate.source_document_title: 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guideline for the Management of Heart Failure; Core Components of Cardiac Rehabilitation Programs: 2024 Update
candidate.source_locator: 2022 AHA/ACC/HFSA Guideline → Section 7.1.3, Management of Stage C HF: Activity, Exercise Prescription, and Cardiac Rehabilitation: exercise training improves functional status, exercise performance, and quality of life; exercise-based cardiac rehabilitation is associated with improved functional capacity/exercise tolerance and reduced overall/HF-specific hospitalization in appropriate HF populations. 2024 AHA/AACVPR Scientific Statement → Top Things to Know items 1-4: cardiac rehabilitation is indicated in a broad cardiovascular population including stable heart failure and includes assessment, risk-factor management, psychosocial care, exercise training, and physical-activity counseling.
candidate.source_organization: American Heart Association/American College of Cardiology/Heart Failure Society of America; American Heart Association/American Association of Cardiovascular and Pulmonary Rehabilitation
candidate.source_version_date: HF guideline 2022-04-01; cardiac-rehabilitation scientific statement updated 2024-09-24
